evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Define and champion the "trust infrastructure" — the testing, data-contract, and observability standards the team works to — that lets the business depend on our models
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by trust infrastructure, testing, data contracts, observability, and correctness ('care about whether the answer is correct, not just whether the code runs') with no velocity-first framing despite an AI-accelerated workflow, giving a clear rigour classification.
evidence.domain_risk: Experience in the insurance sector is a plus. As more of the routine coding becomes AI-assisted, deep domain understanding becomes more of a differentiator, not less
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Zego is a motor insurance company; combined with explicit 'trust infrastructure' and correctness framing around business-critical data models, this places domain risk at high.
evidence.data_team_maturity: We're a small, dynamic team responsible for all aspects of data — availability, quality, integration, problem formulation, success metrics, reporting, and analytics.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Named tools (dbt, Snowflake, Looker) are used in active responsibilities and the team already has established practices (AI-First approach, trust infrastructure) that the candidate extends and sets patterns for — a growing mid-stage team rather than early or fully mature/specialized.
evidence.jd_authorship: Own the design of robust, scalable data models and exposures in dbt, Snowflake, and Looker — and set the patterns and conventions the wider team reuses
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise tools, concrete architectural decisions, and specific AI-workflow context, giving an unusually clear and detailed picture of daily work — hiring_manager authorship.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll own the design of the data models the whole business depends on
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on internal data platform/model ownership and trust infrastructure that the broader business and team rely on, rather than a specific commercial, product, or finance function.
evidence.autonomy_level: You'll own the design of the data models the whole business depends on, set the standards and patterns the rest of the team builds to, and help shape how we put AI to work
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The candidate sets standards, architecture, and direction for the team's AI-assisted workflow — an explicitly strategic framing reinforced by 'technical anchor' and 'set the technical direction others follow'.
evidence.ai_role: Use AI-assisted development to move faster — spending less time hand-writing boilerplate and more time specifying intent, reviewing, and refining
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is explicitly expected to use AI coding tools to accelerate their own SQL/data-modelling work and critically review AI-generated code — the AI is the candidate's own tool, making this ai_user (not ai_enabler, since the infrastructure built isn't described as feeding downstream AI systems).
evidence.testing_framing: Define and champion the "trust infrastructure" — the testing, data-contract, and observability standards the team works to
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data contracts are framed as something the candidate defines and champions, an explicit ownership responsibility rather than a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: care about whether the answer is correct, not just whether the code runs
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High: repeated trust/correctness framing throughout ('trust infrastructure', 'models we can trust', 'whether what we ship is correct and trustworthy') reflects a dominant risk-and-trust register, reinforced by the insurance sector context.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: shaping the structure of a data domain from the ground up
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role mixes owning/extending existing data models and trust infrastructure with shaping new data domains 'from the ground up', giving a mixed signal.
